item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 261132
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll, and
on Tropical Storm Iselle, located well to the west of the southern
tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Central East Pacific (EP93):
A broad area of low pressure located well south of southwestern
Mexico is producing a large area of showers and thunderstorms and is
gradually becoming better organized. Environmental conditions are
expected to support gradual development of this system, and a
tropical depression is likely to form during the next day or so
while it moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, well offshore of
Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Western East Pacific:
An elongated, broad area of low pressure located well to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands is producing disorganized
showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for gradual development of this system, and a tropical depression is
likely to form late this week or early this weekend while the system
drifts to the northeast, then turns westward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form this weekend well to the south
of southwestern Mexico. Environmental conditions appear favorable
for some gradual development of this system, and a tropical
depression could form by early next week while it moves westward to
west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands late this week or over the weekend. Some gradual development
is possible by early next week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Public Advisory Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 261433
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Iselle Advisory Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
800 AM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026
 
...ISELLE WEAKENS...
...FORECAST TO BECOME A POST-TROPICAL CYCLONE TONIGHT...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...22.2N 124.0W
ABOUT 900 MI...1450 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Iselle was 
located near latitude 22.2 North, longitude 124.0 West. Iselle is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h) and this 
general motion is expected to continue over the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Steady weakening is expected, and Iselle is forecast to become a 
post-tropical remnant low by tonight.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 230 miles (370 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Iselle will continue to affect the west
coast of the Baja California Peninsula for a couple more days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 261434
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Iselle Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
800 AM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026
 
Wind shear and dry air continue to take a toll on Iselle this 
morning. The low-level center is fully exposed, with what little 
deep convection remains displaced over 100 n mi to the northeast. 
Earlier scatterometer data indicated winds were still around 40 to 
45 kt. However, given the recent degradation in satellite appearance 
and decreasing subjective and objective intensity estimates, the 
initial intensity is lowered to 40 kt for this advisory.
 
Iselle is expected to continue moving west-northwestward over the 
next few days, steered by a mid-level ridge to the north. Increasing 
wind shear, cooler sea surface temperatures, and a drier air mass 
will continue to weaken the cyclone, and it is likely to become 
devoid of deep convection by tonight. The latest NHC forecast 
follows these trends and indicates Iselle will become a 
post-tropical cyclone tonight. The remnant low is then expected to 
gradually spin down and open into a trough by day 3. The track and 
intensity forecasts are similar to the previous advisory, with only 
minor adjustments made toward the consensus aids.
